doc.title: Bobby Shew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 1, 2020

title: Quickly becoming busy in L.A. studios through Chuck Findley
summary: Chuck Findley and others who knew Shew from Buddy's and Woody's bands send him sessions, and he is booked daily within two weeks.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And then Chuck Findley was in the trumpet section and he — and Chuck — I had gotten Chuck on Buddy Rich’s band when he was just out of high school. And so Chuck said, “Bobby, what are you doing? Are you going to stay here?” “Yeah, we moved here.” He says, “Well man I’ve got a bunch of dates I need you on.” All of a sudden Chuck was double booked and he was sending me in to cover for him on things and I’d show up, I was doing, like within two weeks in L.A. I was like doing a session or two almost every day. I was suddenly busy. And guys would look at me and go didn’t you just move to town? How are you so busy all of a sudden you know? I said, “The phone just keeps ringing.”
You should have just said, “Well it’s talent man, come on.”

Yeah. No I wouldn’t do that. No the thing was they’d got me in and people like Chuck and then John Audino and Ray Triscari, all these guys had known me through Buddy’s band and through Woody’s band and through things like that, they knew who I was. And so they said, “Hell yes.” And the contractors said okay. And of course when you show up you’ve got to play and I could read really well and I had decent chops. I had limitations but I didn’t let anybody know what they were you know.
